F1.title: artifact publication destroys the previous artifact on a refused re-probe
F1.root_cause: publish renamed over the previous inode before the re-probe; retract knew only the staged name
F1.fix: jobs/feature_verification.py: publish keeps the previous artifact as `<stem>.extracted.txt.prev` (os.link, copy2 fallback) before os.replace; retract restores it atomically after a post-publication refusal (or removes the refused bytes when there was none); new finalize() drops .prev only after the fenced COMPLETED commit; ArtifactPublication gained optional `finalize`

F2.title: cancel / reclaim race — a stale worker could reopen or settle a newer execution
F2.root_cause: `_mark_pending` was `WHERE id=?` only; `_mark_completed/_failed/_verifying` were status-conditioned but not owner-conditioned
F2.fix: jobs/lifecycle.ExecutionClaim(job_id, attempt) minted by the PENDING-only reservation CAS; every worker-side UPDATE adds `AND attempt = ?` and returns rowcount == 1; `(PROCESSING, PROCESSING)` edge removed from TRANSITIONS
F2.old_red: test_t1 @947173c: `PENDING is COMPLETED` (cancelled worker reopened a completed newer execution); test_t2/t3 analogous

F3.title: durable completion vs notification
F3.root_cause: `_mark_completed` returned None; `_notify_completion` fired unconditionally after it
F3.fix: fenced CAS returns bool; success/failure hooks fire only when the UPDATE committed (rowcount == 1); a rejected transition logs `job_transition_rejected` and announces nothing. Contract decided as 'never lie' (not 'eventual delivery'); transactional outbox rejected (D-0016)
F3.old_red: test_t15 @947173c: `['me'] == []` (✅ hook fired with no COMPLETED row)

F4_R5.title: concurrent workers — two processes own one execution
F4_R5.root_cause: reservation `WHERE status IN ('pending','processing')`, no rowcount check
F4_R5.fix: reservation is `WHERE status = 'pending'` + rowcount check; takeover only via resume_pending (startup: rows not executing in this process; expiry: `stale_after` window)

known_residuals: Publication fence window: ownership is re-read immediately before os.replace; between that read and the rename the filesystem checks no token. Entering it requires a takeover (resume_pending) in that interval — not a concurrent reservation. Documented JOB_LIFECYCLE.md §2a; closing it needs token-aware storage (out of scope, D-0016).
Handler-side writes of workspace-scoped lanes (creative_render / slideshow_render / story) are key-scoped and handler-owned; the queue fences only its own publication lane.
Notification is 'never lie', not 'eventual delivery': a crash between the fenced commit and the hook loses that one notification; durable state stays true.
story output_path durability: dispatch-time path is not receipt-validated (carried over, unchanged).
